newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, BOJ back to neutral.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, BOJ back to neutral.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended the day session on Monday firmer, while the Bank of Japan returned to a neutral money market stance after accommodative operations since February 28, traders said.
In its regular morning operation, the BOJ showed its "reserve neutral" stance by fully offsetting a projected 300 billion yen surplus.

Traders said the BOJ felt comfortable returning to a neutral position after the key call rate fell as low as 0.45 percent on Friday due to its accommodative stance over that week. The call rate was traded at 0.48-49 percent on Monday.
But upward pressure on rates in the short end of the money market still exists as banks' demand to raise funds in the overnight call market remained strong, traders said.
Traders forecast the overnight call rate would move in a range of 0.46-0.52 percent in a runup to the final day of the one-month bank reserves reporting period on Friday.

In the United States, after stronger than expected February jobs data, some economists are forecasting that the Federal Reserve will raise its target for the federal funds rate, currently at 5.25 percent, by 25 basis points on March 25.
"Japan is unlikely to follow a U.S. lead and tighten credit despite signs of economic recovery here," said Shoji Kitta, president of Totan Research Co Ltd.
This is because of the remaining fragility of Japan's banking system and the political incentive to aid banks through ultra-low interest rates that make banks' bad loan write-offs easier, Kitta said.
On the TIFFE, traders are waiting for January machinery orders due on Tuesday for the next trading signal.
Despite the small gains on Monday, sentiment in the Euroyen futures market has been basically bearish due to selling interest partly by foreign accounts, traders said.
"If machinery orders are better than expected, traders would use them as a good excuse to build fresh short positions," said a European bank trader.
Traders forecast the key December Euroyen would move in a range of 99.17-99.23 this week.
